title: the provenance index equals the audit chain after a downgrade
note: basis 'shown' means shown by the card's unit test on the test cluster (a real drain, the real index, pg_dump and pg_restore), failing on the base and passing with the change; the walk's box was not read.

findings.claim: after a downgrade or rollback restored the database, the drain recorded the journal resync but never wrote back the index rows of the lines drained since the rollback point, so they stayed missing until a rebuild by hand
the drain decided once at its start whether the index was installed, so tables made by the role script on a running box were not written until the drain restarted

lines drained before the index's tables existed are written only by trialbox provenance --rebuild, and no role of a compose box can run that rebuild whole: tb_orchestrator reads the register but not writes the index, tb_audit_writer writes it but cannot read the register or delete, and the admin role is reached only through psql

an update's rollback restores the whole trial database from its dump, the opt-out register with it, so an opt-out recorded after the dump and its erasures are lost, with no list, audit or hold as a backup restore has (D-493, D-522)
